newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks roar to 7th straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks roar to 7th straight record close.

text.p: Bulls unleashed in recent sessions again charged higher on the Mexican bourse, giving it its seventh record close in a row on Thursday.
Analysts and dealers said a recent crop of positive economic news continued to grab the interest of domestic and foreign investors, as a strong Dow Jones provided a tailwind.
"It's like crazy down here, there's a loads of foreigners and we're snowed under with orders," a floor trader said.
Final closing prices showed the blue chip IPC share index climbed 72.15 points, or 1.69 percent, to a new closing and trading record of 4,353.67.
The previous record of 4,281.52 points was set on Wednesday. Heavy trading volume of 138.8 million shares evidenced the strong presence of investors.
"The string of good news underpins the domestic fundamentals behind companies," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
"The most important items have been industrial activity, unemployment and the pre-payment," he added. "And, of course, the international backdrop couldn't be better."
The Finance Ministry announced a stronger-than-expected year-on-year rise in industrial activity for April on Tuesday.
Also on Tuesday, the Finance Ministry announced it would prepay an entire $600 million medium-term bank note issue.
On Wednesday, the National Statistics Institute reported a sharp drop in the open unemployment rate.
The Dow Jones industrial average surged 58.35 points to 7,777.06, while the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 4/32 to yield 6.68 percent.
Dealers said market heavyweight Telmex led the rally. Telmex L shares climbed 28 centavos to 18.80 pesos, while the telecom's ADRs ended up 1/2 47-1/4.
Telmex accounted for 8 percent of all shares traded.
Dealers noted demand was also heavy for corn flour and tortilla company Maseca, up 64 centavos to 8.74 pesos, and cable maker Grupo Industrial Camesa, which gained 15 centavos to 4.90 pesos.
"It's mainly technical. Camesa and Maseca had lagged the market," Rojas said.
Cement stocks had a good day, dealers said, because a breakdown of Tuesday's industrial output data showed construction activity had been strong.

Analysts said cement makers tended to outperform large construction stocks, because a lot of building in Mexico is done by small or even informal firms that, although not listed, buy small bags of cement from large companies.
Cement maker Cemex rose 95 centavos to 33.20 pesos, while its sector stablemate Apasco ended up 2.40 pesos to 54.00 pesos.
Lazard Freres announced in early trade it was initiating coverage of Cemex with a buy recommendation, while it rated Apasco a hold.
Dealers and analysts noted the financial sector did not share the market bonanza due to profit-taking after they had recently far outperformed the market.
Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, saw its B shares end down 2 centavos at 3.80 pesos, while its A shares shed 1 centavo to 2.17 pesos.
Financials also crowded the top of the prominent sliders' list.
Rojas noted heavy demand for an initial public offering by paging company Biper was a sign of healthy market liquidity.
"Appetite among foreign investors for relatively small placements is a good sign," he said.
Biper placed 205 million pesos ($25.8 million) of B shares at a price of 2.75 pesos each. The shares rose 43 centavos to close at 3.18 pesos on demand, traders said.
"Amazing. As they went public on open outcry, they were snapped up," a floor trader said.
On the broad market, of 122 stocks traded, gainers heavily outnumbered sliders by 76 to 18.
(( -- Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
